corpusSummary: The corpus presents a cautious, cross-disciplinary view of large language models in 2026, emphasizing how users trust, adopt, and interact with AI across education, health, and governance contexts, while researchers test LLMs as analytical collaborators, assess safety and bias, and explore ethical frameworks. It also foregrounds equity, literacy, and transparent governance as essential complements to technical potentials.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction and social dynamics
themes.description: Across the records, studies investigate how users trust, prefer AI representations, adopt AI tools, and navigate embodiment and social influence in education, health, and daily decision-making.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools and analytical collaborators
themes.description: A range of papers propone LLMs as analytical partners for coding, framing, data extraction, design ideation, and cross-domain simulation, highlighting methodological opportunities and governance needs.

themes.name: Safety, bias, and misinformation in AI-enabled communication
themes.description: The corpus underscores concerns about bias, misinformation propagation, safety of AI-generated content (especially in health), and the need for transparency and governance to mitigate harms.

themes.name: AI in education and learning
themes.description: Numerous studies examine AI’s role in pedagogy, literacy development, assessment integrity, and learner engagement across K–12, higher education, and lifelong learning, noting both opportunities and risks.

themes.name: Equity, inclusion, and governance in AI deployment
themes.description: The records reveal disparities in access and adoption (digital divide, global south contexts) and call for governance, standards, and ethical scrutiny to ensure fair, responsible AI deployment.
